chunks: Do not think that the disbelievers will be mighty on earth; and their abode is the Fire, and evil is the destination.

key_terms.وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ: And their abode is the Fire

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the fate of disbelievers on earth and in the hereafter?
ai.summary: In Surah An-Nur, this verse serves as a reassurance to the faithful during the early Medinan period, countering the arrogance of polytheists who believed their temporal power on earth made them invincible. Shia exegetes emphasize that 'escaping' (mu'jizin) refers to evading divine justice through worldly dominance, yet their ultimate return (masir) to Hellfire underscores the certainty of the Hereafter. This highlights the transient nature of worldly power compared to the eternal reality of divine retribution.
